title: Return 0 from timers on a `Window` whose document isn't fully active
body: Return 0 from timers on a `Window` whose document isn't fully active This also skips the Trusted Types check, so the default policy doesn't run. Fixes #13019. - [ ] At least two implementers are interested (and none opposed): * Mozilla * … - [x] [Tests](https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt) are written and can be reviewed and commented upon at: * https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/pull/63202 - [x] [Implementation bugs](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) are filed: * Chromium: https://issues.chromium.org/issues/568348285 * Gecko: https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=2077381 * WebKit: https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=326040 * Deno: N/A (`Window` only) * Node.js: N/A (`Window` only) - [x] Corresponding [HTML AAM](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/) & [ARIA in HTML](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/) issues & PRs: N/A - [ ] [MDN issue](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/MAINTAINERS.md#handling-pull-requests) is filed: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/setTimeout#return_value could say that 0 can be returned (and when) - [x] The top of this comment includes a [clear commit message](https://github.com/whatwg/meta/blob/main/COMMITTING.md) to use.
